prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed heterobifunctional molecules bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase and so destroy it.

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as my preferred single achievement. Event-driven pharmacology through induced proximity is a new chemical design principle: linker, ligand and ternary-complex design are explicit chemistry, and the approach has reached proteins once called undruggable. The 2001 PROTAC proposal by Crews and Deshaies is the conceptual origin, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the idea rational and drug-like. VHL and cereblon mechanisms have been reproduced in many independent laboratories. The chair's summary confirms that B026 is the one candidate that appears in all eight round-1 files, so even where members decline to rank it first, none disputes the science. I am restricting the citation to the designed-degrader concept, which keeps one discovery under one citation and keeps the configuration to three names.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, so clinical proof is pending and recognition may be early, which is the objection that moved Aqvist, Chabes, Linke and Sparr to alternatives. The glue strand (Handa, Ito, and the cereblon work by Gray and others) is also left outside a Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli citation, and this will read as an omission to anyone who treats degraders and glues as one field. Support is broad but shallow: two preferred configurations in round 1, with different third names.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that cereblon identification explained thalidomide and created the glue strand, and says he would not oppose Ciulli on a pure PROTAC citation.
responses.response: We now agree that the third name is the only live difference between us, and that either is defensible. I keep Ciulli because the citation I propose is about designed heterobifunctional degraders, where Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are the rational-design step, whereas Handa's work is target identification for a drug class that already existed. I also note that the Handa citation needs a wider wording that covers glues, and that wording invites the Ito, Gray and Kim question Brzezinski himself raised. If the committee prefers the wider induced-proximity citation, I would accept Handa and not make it a point of principle.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B065 with Buchwald and Hartwig, argues that C-N coupling needed a new ligand-controlled mechanistic framework distinct from the 2010 C-C coupling prize, and treats Kosugi as a citation-wording matter.
responses.response: That answers my round-1 worry only in part. The mechanistic argument about amide-bound palladium intermediates and difficult reductive elimination is persuasive and I now see B065 as more than an extension of the 2010 prize. I also agree that Kosugi does not justify a third name. I still place conceptual novelty on the side of B026, because it adds a pharmacological modality rather than a better way to make a known bond type, but I move B065 to my first alternative and would vote for it without hesitation if B026 were not available. Our disagreement is now mainly about weighing maturity against novelty.

responses.point: Chabes would wait for a PROTAC approval before placing degraders above a field with 25 years of confirmed use, and says any three names split one joint field between PROTAC and cereblon discoverers.
responses.response: I take the maturity argument seriously and I have not dismissed it. My answer is that the prize criterion is the discovery, not the first marketed drug: the principle is confirmed by independent laboratories, by structural work on ternary complexes and by many clinical-stage molecules, and thalidomide-class drugs already show the biology works in patients. On the split-field point I partly concede: the honest reading is two strands, and I have narrowed my citation to the designed-degrader strand so that the three names are consistent with it. I do not believe waiting for an approval would change the scientific merit, but I accept it would change how many colleagues are willing to vote now.

responses.point: Linke prefers B037 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman, as sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators and clonal arrays, and weights the proven maturity of sequencing over the promise of degraders.
responses.response: The narrowing to the Solexa pair addresses most of what I objected to in round 1, since it removes Mayer and takes Rothberg and Ju out of the three-name allocation, and I treat B037 as a real alternative. What remains for me is category: the citation rests on terminators and surface chemistry, yet the prize-relevant impact is in genomics, and the 1980 sequencing prize makes the claim harder. I weigh that more than the maturity gap with degraders, but I recognise the maturity point is a genuine one and it is why B037 is my second alternative.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B065, and questions whether a second synthetic-methodology prize is wise, and also wants native chemical ligation kept alive.
responses.response: As the member closest to synthetic methodology he gives the strongest case that B065 is the safe choice, and I accept the attribution is the cleanest on the table. I do not find his concern about two methodology awards relevant to my position, because my single-part preference is not a methodology prize. On native chemical ligation, I still regard it as strong and mature chemistry, but with a six-name allocation and no second part in my configuration I am not moving it into my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will recognise degraders before an approved PROTAC drug, and whether any colleague preferring B065 or B037 would move on that point.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the right third name, and whether a PROTAC and glue two-part structure would be better; a second part would exceed the three-person cap given my current names.
My account of the clinical status of degraders rests on recollection and not on verified records; the supplied files do not independently settle priority among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa and Ito.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I work in peptide-based biomaterials and biosensing at Linkoping University and have no documented tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa or the other credited names. My profile records a research overlap with Emma Sparr (self-assembly), which does not bear on this configuration. No disclosure has changed since round 1.
